text.p: Yugoslav President Zoran Lilic congratulated U.S. President Bill Clinton on Wednesday, saying his reelection would mean a boost in bilateral ties, the Yugoslav news agency Tanjug reported.

"Lilic expressed the belief that the United States would continue its policy of good cooperation between the two countries in the implementation of the peace process and strengthening the traditionally friendly (bilateral) relations," Tanjug said, quoting the presidential information service.
Clinton's sweeping re-election victory on Wednesday over Republican Bob Dole was good news for Belgrade which has backed the Dayton peace process engineered by his administration.

"New people in the White House would certainly have affected U.S. policy on Bosnia and the region on the whole. That would not be good news since the peace process is still fragile," a source close to the Yugoslav government said.

Clinton helped to launch the Dayton peace plan and put pressure on the warring factions to sign the peace accord in Dayton, Ohio, in November 1995, ending a 43-month war in Bosnia and paving the way for stabilisation in the Balkans.

Ties between Yugoslavia, which comprises Serbia and Montenegro, and the United States improved after Serbia's President Slobodan Milosevic forced the Bosnian Serbs to accept the peace plan and made peace with Bosnia and Croatia this year.
Milosevic's leftist coalition won federal elections last Sunday and his aides have said this has secured his powerbase for further implementation of the Dayton peace accord.
